investigationEvent.text: Patient T.P. (male, 55 years) was treated with Testdrugimab 200mg daily for rheumatoid arthritis starting 2026-01-15. On 2026-03-01, nausea developed (resolved by 2026-03-10). On 2026-03-05, hepatic enzyme elevation was noted; ALT 850 U/L (normal 7-40), AST 760 U/L (normal 10-40). Drug was withdrawn. Patient developed progressive hepatic failure and died on 2026-03-12. Autopsy not performed. Medical history: hypertension (ongoing). Past drug: Ibuprofen 2020-2023 for RA. Concomitant: Lisinopril and Methotrexate. Sender diagnosis: Hepatic failure.

observationEvent.value: A 55-year-old male with hypertension was initiated on Testdrugimab 200mg daily for rheumatoid arthritis. He had previously taken ibuprofen (2020-2023) which caused gastritis. On day 45 of treatment he developed nausea (resolved day 54) and markedly elevated liver enzymes (ALT 850 U/L, AST 760 U/L; bilirubin 4.8 mg/dL). Drug was discontinued. Despite cessation, the patient progressed to hepatic failure and died on 2026-03-12. Reporter concludes Testdrugimab was the likely cause of drug-induced hepatic failure.
